sources.entry: Keeper.sh - Calendar syncing tool that pulls and pushes events between calendar sources and destinations via iCal/ICS or OAuth, with support for anonymized busy/free events. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Keeper.sh is an AGPL-3.0 calendar syncing tool that pulls events from Google, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail, CalDAV, or iCal/ICS links and pushes them to other calendars so busy times line up.
summary.what_it_does: Keeper.sh reads events from source calendars (Google, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail, CalDAV, and remote iCal/ICS links) and writes them to destination calendars so time slots align across all of them. Google, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail and CalDAV can be sources or destinations, while iCal/ICS links are pull-only. Per-source privacy settings can strip event names, descriptions and locations, replacing titles with a calendar or event name template. It tracks mappings so events deleted at the source are removed from destinations, and its cleanup only touches events it created. It also exposes a combined iCal feed, a REST API under /api/v1 authenticated by API tokens, and an MCP server with tools for listing, creating, updating, deleting and RSVPing to events, finding free time, and triggering or pausing sync.
use_cases: combine work, personal and business calendars into one view
stop meetings overlapping across several calendars
share busy/free status without event details
subscribe to one combined iCal feed from any calendar app
let an AI agent read or manage calendar events via MCP
self-host a calendar sync service with Docker
how_to_run: Self-hosting: run the keeper-standalone:2 Docker image behind a reverse proxy (recommended starting point)
Generate a .env with BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and ENCRYPTION_KEY using openssl rand -base64 32
Set TRUSTED_ORIGINS if accessing from a URL other than the configured one
Optionally set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET and MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID/SECRET for those integrations
Development: bun install, generate and trust a local root CA, then bun dev (requires Bun 1.3.11+ and Docker)
notable: Incremental sync for Google and Outlook using provider sync tokens and delta links
Optional realtime push via WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_URL, with polling as the default
Deletion tracking via mapping rows so remote copies are removed later; cleanup only touches events Keeper.sh created
Built-in OIDC SSO support (Authentik, Keycloak, Pocket ID, etc.) and optional disabling of local auth
Official hosted version at keeper.sh; self-hosting includes all Pro features
caveats: Google and Microsoft destinations require you to register your own OAuth apps when self-hosting
Self-hosting means you handle the server, domain, upgrades, backups and maintenance
Free hosted tier is limited: 2 linked accounts, 3 sync mappings, 30-minute refresh, 25 API requests per day
